subChunks.title: Transitions and Animations
subChunks.hookHtml: The difference between a UI that feels polished and one that feels cheap is often just a 150ms transition. Without one, hover states snap, buttons teleport, and modals pop in jarringly. Tailwind provides transition, duration, and easing utilities — plus four built-in animations for common patterns like loading states and notification indicators.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
The fundamental rule — transition goes on the BASE state

/* WRONG — transition on hover state (forward works, reverse snaps) */
class="bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 hover:transition-colors"

/* CORRECT — transition on the base element */
class="bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 transition-colors duration-150"

The transition must be present in both states for it to work in both directions. On the hover state, it only applies entering — the reverse snap is instant.

Transition utilities

transition            /* transitions all commonly animated properties */
transition-colors     /* only color, bg, border, fill, stroke — most performant for buttons */
transition-transform  /* only transform — use for scale/rotate effects */
transition-opacity    /* only opacity */
transition-shadow     /* only box-shadow */
transition-none       /* disable all transitions */

Duration and easing

duration-75    /* 75ms  — near-instant */
duration-100   /* 100ms — fast */
duration-150   /* 150ms — standard for interactive UI */
duration-200   /* 200ms */
duration-300   /* 300ms — modals, panels */
duration-500   /* 500ms — hero transitions */

ease-linear    /* constant speed */
ease-in        /* slow start, fast end */
ease-out       /* fast start, slow end — entering elements */
ease-in-out    /* slow start, slow end — most natural */

Transform utilities

scale-95         /* 95% — pressed/active state */
scale-105        /* 105% — hovered card lift */
rotate-180       /* 180 degrees — accordion arrow flip */
-translate-y-1   /* shift up 4px — subtle card lift */
translate-x-full /* shift fully right — slide out */

Built-in animations

animate-spin    /* 360deg rotation loop — loading spinners */
animate-pulse   /* opacity 0.5 ↔ 1 loop — skeleton loading screens */
animate-bounce  /* bouncing Y-axis — scroll indicators */
animate-ping    /* scale 1→2 with opacity fade — notification dots */

Practical examples

/* Loading spinner */
<svg class="animate-spin h-5 w-5 text-white">...</svg>

/* Skeleton loading line */
<div class="h-4 bg-gray-200 rounded animate-pulse"></div>

/* Notification badge with ping */
<span class="relative flex h-2 w-2">
  <span class="animate-ping absolute inline-flex h-full w-full rounded-full bg-red-400 opacity-75"></span>
  <span class="relative inline-flex rounded-full h-2 w-2 bg-red-500"></span>
</span>

Accessibility — always add reduced motion

motion-safe:animate-bounce     /* only animates if user HASN'T requested reduced motion */
motion-reduce:transition-none  /* disables transitions for users who have */
motion-reduce:animate-none     /* disables animations for users who have */

This is a WCAG requirement. Some users experience nausea or seizure risk from motion. Always add motion-reduce: to looping or attention-grabbing animations.

Sable: "One hundred and fifty milliseconds, ease-in-out — that is the difference between a button that feels alive and one that feels painted on a wall. And remember: motion-reduce:transition-none. Always. Some readers cannot tolerate motion. Ignoring them is not craft. It is negligence."

storyBeats.speaker: Sable the Illuminator
storyBeats.text: The snap is cheap. The breath is craft. One hundred and fifty milliseconds, ease-in-out — that is the difference between a button that feels alive and one that feels painted on a wall.

storyBeats.speaker: Transition on the base state (correct pattern)
storyBeats.text:
<!-- CORRECT: transition on the element, hover changes the value -->
<button class="bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 active:scale-95
               transition-all duration-150 ease-in-out
               motion-reduce:transition-none">
  Submit
</button>

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build an animated interactive button and a skeleton loading card:

  • .btn-primary: inline-flex, items-center, gap-2, px-5, py-2.5, bg-blue-600, hover:bg-blue-700, active:scale-95, text-white, text-sm, font-medium, rounded-lg, transition-all, duration-150, ease-in-out, motion-reduce:transition-none
  • .spinner: animate-spin, h-4, w-4
  • .skeleton-line: h-4, bg-gray-200, rounded, animate-pulse
subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build an animated notification bell from scratch. The bell should animate-bounce with a red badge counter positioned absolutely in the corner. Add a transition-all wrapper so the component fades when toggled. Include motion-reduce:animate-none on any animated element.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Why does the transition utility need to be on the base state rather than the hover state? What happens to the transition if you put it only on hover:? Explain what each of the four built-in animations (spin, pulse, bounce, ping) does and give one real UI use case for each.

questions.prompt: Which animation class creates a repeating scale-and-fade effect, commonly used for notification dot indicators?
questions.explanation: animate-ping scales an element up while fading it out, creating a ripple/radar effect. It's the standard pattern for the pulsing notification dot. animate-pulse is for skeleton loading screens, animate-spin for spinners, and animate-bounce for vertical bouncing.

questions.prompt: A loading indicator is an SVG that should spin continuously. Which class produces this effect?
questions.explanation: animate-spin applies a continuous 360-degree rotation animation (spin 1s linear infinite). It is the standard class for loading spinners in Tailwind.

questions.prompt: A developer applies hover:transition-colors hover:duration-200 hover:bg-blue-700 to a button. When testing, the forward hover transition works, but when the cursor leaves, the background snaps back instantly. What is the bug?
options: The transition utilities are on the hover state — when the cursor leaves and the hover state is removed, the transition is removed too, so the reverse change is instant. Fix: move transition-colors and duration-200 to the base element
hover: variants don't support transitions — use JavaScript for transitions
duration-200 needs to also be on the base element but transition-colors can stay on hover:
The browser doesn't support reverse transitions — add transition-reverse class
questions.answer: The transition utilities are on the hover state — when the cursor leaves and the hover state is removed, the transition is removed too, so the reverse change is instant. Fix: move transition-colors and duration-200 to the base element
questions.explanation: CSS transitions must be present on the element in both states for the transition to work in both directions. If transition-colors is only under hover:, the browser adds the transition when the mouse enters (forward works) but removes it when the mouse leaves (reverse snaps). Moving transition-colors duration-200 to the base class fixes both directions.
